en.title: Fed holds rates steady as Warsh changes interest-rate approach
en.dek: The Federal Reserve kept its benchmark rate at 3.75%‑4.00% while Chair Jerome Warsh announced a shift in the Fed’s rate‑setting methodology.
facts: The Federal Reserve kept its target range at 3.75%‑4.00% on 29 October 2026 (Hardware Retailing, WTVC).
MarketWatch and Conduit Street Blog said the Fed’s policy rate was unchanged on that day.
The personal consumption expenditures price index rose to 3.7% in September 2026 (The Guardian, MarketWatch).
The Hill and the New York Times reported the PCE index increased in September after a decline in August.
Yahoo Finance and Morningstar reported the European Central Bank left its interest rates unchanged.
WPEC and KATU reported Chair Jerome Warsh announced a change to the Fed’s rate‑setting approach.
body: Chair Jerome Warsh said the Federal Reserve will change the way it sets interest rates, according to WPEC and KATU. He also announced that the Fed kept its target range at 3.75% to 4.00% on Wednesday, as reported by Hardware Retailing and WTVC.
The Federal Reserve kept its policy rate unchanged on Wednesday, MarketWatch reported. Conduit Street Blog confirmed the decision maintained the target range at its current level.
September data show the personal consumption expenditures price index rose to 3.7%, The Guardian noted. MarketWatch added that the cost of living increased sharply last month.
The Hill reported that the PCE index increased in September after falling in August. The New York Times described the change as a slight acceleration in inflation.
The European Central Bank left its interest rates unchanged, Yahoo Finance reported. Morningstar corroborated the decision and cited an energy‑price shock as a factor.
The Fed uses the PCE index as its preferred inflation gauge, The Hill explained. The index is released each month by the Bureau of Economic Analysis.
MarketWatch said the Fed’s pause on rate hikes may not last as inflation pressures remain elevated. The outlet noted that the new approach announced by Warsh could influence future policy decisions.
en.context: The Federal Reserve uses the personal consumption expenditures price index, published monthly by the Bureau of Economic Analysis, as its preferred measure of inflation (The Hill).

de.title: Fed lässt Zinsen unverändert, während Warsh Ansatz zur Zinspolitik ändert
de.dek: Die Federal Reserve behielt ihren Leitzins bei 3,75 % bis 4,00 % bei, während Vorsitzender Jerome Warsh eine Änderung der Methodik der Fed zur Zinsfestlegung bekannt gab.
facts: Die Federal Reserve behielt ihre Zielspanne am 29. Oktober 2026 bei 3,75 % bis 4,00 % bei (Hardware Retailing, WTVC).
MarketWatch und der Conduit Street Blog teilten mit, dass der Leitzins der Fed an diesem Tag unverändert blieb.
Der Preisindex für die persönlichen Konsumausgaben stieg im September 2026 auf 3,7 % (The Guardian, MarketWatch).
The Hill und die New York Times berichteten, dass der PCE-Index im September nach einem Rückgang im August anstieg.
Yahoo Finance und Morningstar berichteten, dass die Europäische Zentralbank ihre Zinssätze unverändert ließ.
WPEC und KATU berichteten, dass Vorsitzender Jerome Warsh eine Änderung des Ansatzes der Fed zur Zinsfestlegung ankündigte.
body: Vorsitzender Jerome Warsh erklärte, dass die Federal Reserve die Art und Weise der Zinsfestlegung ändern werde, so WPEC und KATU. Er gab zudem bekannt, dass die Fed ihre Zielspanne am Mittwoch bei 3,75 % bis 4,00 % beließ, wie Hardware Retailing und WTVC berichteten.
Die Federal Reserve ließ ihren Leitzins am Mittwoch unverändert, berichtete MarketWatch. Der Conduit Street Blog bestätigte, dass die Entscheidung die Zielspanne auf ihrem aktuellen Niveau hielt.

Daten aus dem September zeigen, dass der Preisindex für die persönlichen Konsumausgaben auf 3,7 % stieg, stellte The Guardian fest. MarketWatch fügte hinzu, dass die Lebenshaltungskosten im letzten Monat stark gestiegen seien.
The Hill berichtete, dass der PCE-Index im September nach einem Rückgang im August anstieg. Die New York Times beschrieb die Änderung als eine leichte Beschleunigung der Inflation.
Die Europäische Zentralbank ließ ihre Zinssätze unverändert, berichtete Yahoo Finance. Morningstar bestätigte die Entscheidung und nannte einen Energiepreisschock als Faktor.
Die Fed nutzt den PCE-Index als ihren bevorzugten Inflationsindikator, erklärte The Hill. Der Index wird jeden Monat vom Bureau of Economic Analysis veröffentlicht.

MarketWatch erklärte, dass die Pause der Fed bei den Zinserhöhungen möglicherweise nicht anhalten werde, da der Inflationsdruck erhöht bleibe. Das Medium merkte an, dass der von Warsh angekündigte neue Ansatz künftige politische Entscheidungen beeinflussen könnte.
de.context: Die Federal Reserve nutzt den monatlich vom Bureau of Economic Analysis veröffentlichten Preisindex für die persönlichen Konsumausgaben als ihr bevorzugtes Maß für die Inflation (The Hill).

body: Jerome Warsh said the Federal Reserve will modify the way it sets interest rates, according to WPEC and KATU. The announcement came on the same day the Fed released its policy decision.
The Federal Reserve kept its policy rate unchanged on Wednesday, MarketWatch reported and Conduit Street Blog confirmed. The decision maintained the target range at its current level.
The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index rose to 3.7% in September, The Guardian noted. MarketWatch added that the cost of living rose sharply again last month.
The Hill and the New York Times reported that the PCE index increased in September after a decline in August. Both outlets said the change reflects a slight acceleration in inflation.
The European Central Bank also left its interest rates unchanged, Yahoo Finance reported and Morningstar corroborated. The ECB cited an energy‑price shock as a factor in its decision.
MarketWatch said the Fed’s pause on rate hikes may not last as prices continue to rise. The outlet noted that inflation pressures remain elevated.
The Federal Reserve uses the PCE index as its preferred measure of inflation, the Hill explained. The index is released monthly by the Bureau of Economic Analysis.

The personal consumption expenditures index rose to 3.7% in September (The Guardian, MarketWatch).
The PCE index increased in September after falling in August (The Hill, New York Times).
The European Central Bank left its interest rates unchanged (Yahoo Finance, Morningstar).
Jerome Warsh announced a change to the Fed’s rate‑setting approach (WPEC, KATU).

de.title: Fed hält die Zinssätze am Mittwoch unverändert

en.dek: The Federal Reserve left its policy rate unchanged on Wednesday after the personal consumption expenditures index rose to 3.7% in September.
body: The Federal Reserve kept its policy rate unchanged on Wednesday. According to MarketWatch and Conduit Street Blog, the Fed held rates steady at the current level.
The decision followed a series of rate hikes earlier in the year. According to Conduit Street Blog, the Fed had raised rates in September.
The pause came after the personal consumption expenditures price index rose to 3.7% in September. According to The Guardian and MarketWatch, the PCE inflation index increased to 3.7% in September.
The index had fallen in August. According to The Hill and the New York Times, the PCE index fell in August before rising in September.
The PCE is the Fed's preferred measure of inflation. According to the Bureau of Economic Analysis, the PCE tracks changes in consumer prices.
The Fed said it will monitor economic data closely. According to the Fed, the decision reflects recent inflation data.
Market watchers note that the pause may not last as prices continue to rise. According to MarketWatch, the Fed's pause on rate hikes may not last as prices continue to rise.
The European Central Bank also left its rates unchanged. According to Yahoo Finance and Morningstar, the ECB left its rates unchanged.

PCE inflation index rose to 3.7% in September
PCE inflation index fell in August
Fed had raised rates in September
